# Ball Movement 🏃

#### Course: Brick Breaker with JavaScript

## Ball Movement 🏃

Each frame, the ball moves by adding its velocity to its position:

```javascriptDOM
this.x += this.ballSpeedX;
this.y += this.ballSpeedY;
```

ballSpeedX and ballSpeedY are pixels per frame.At 60fps and a speed of 4.5, the ball travels 270 pixels per second. Fast enough to feel responsive, slow enough to track visually.

When the ball reaches a wall, you reverse the velocity for that direction. Left and right walls flip ballSpeedX. The top wall flips ballSpeedY.

There is one detail worth pausing on. Before flipping the direction, you reposition the ball back inside the boundary first:

```javascriptDOM
// Bounce off left wall

if (this.x - this.radius < 0) {
  this.x = this.radius;                        // push back inside boundary
  this.ballSpeedX = Math.abs(this.ballSpeedX); // ensure positive direction
}
```

Without that repositioning step, the ball can clip the wall and bounce repeatedly in the same spot instead of moving on.

![Ball Movement](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

The bottom wall has no bounce. Falling through is how the player loses a life. You will handle that later.

Next, you will add movement to the Ball class and wire up the full game loop so the ball actually starts moving on screen.
